title: COFOG-normalized cross-jurisdiction comparison (only where valid)
context: Cross-jurisdiction budget comparisons are misleading when accounting bases (GASB vs IPSAS), fiscal years, or nominal/real bases differ. COFOG (UN Classification of the Functions of Government) provides a principled functional-category framework that enables valid comparisons across jurisdictions — but only where the mapping is valid and the bases align. This backlog task extends the pipeline to support COFOG-normalized cross-jurisdiction comparisons behind the comparison guardrails (task 013), publishing only when bases are confirmed compatible.
objective: Implement COFOG-normalized cross-jurisdiction budget comparison support behind the comparison guardrails, so that comparisons are only published when accounting bases, fiscal years, and nominal/real bases are confirmed compatible — and blocked or annotated otherwise.
acceptanceCriteria: COFOG functional-category normalization implemented for budget lines where COFOG mapping is valid and recorded

Cross-jurisdiction comparisons using COFOG normalization are only published when accounting bases (e.g., GASB vs IPSAS), fiscal years, and nominal/real bases are confirmed compatible by the comparison guardrails (task 013)
Comparisons blocked or annotated when bases are incompatible; no comparison is silently published across mismatched accounting bases
COFOG mapping is recorded as provenance (which lines were mapped, which standard version) and is not silently assumed
Tested on fixtures covering valid and invalid cross-jurisdiction comparison scenarios
Reviewed and signed off by the public-finance expert; PR merged with green CI and maintainer review passed
output: A merged PR adding COFOG-normalized cross-jurisdiction comparison support behind the comparison guardrails, with COFOG mapping recorded as provenance and comparisons published only where bases are confirmed compatible.
